objective: Add Codex auto-review to HolyAgent's Codex provider for Pi, reproducing Codex's guardian behaviour, as its own capability that can be turned off.
scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-autoreview, branch release/0.3.1/feat/auto-review cut from release/0.3.1/feat/screen at 91d9eb07. The Codex provider lives in packages/integrations/pi/src/codex.ts (registerCodex, CodexSettings) and packages/runtime/src/pi/codex/ (routes.ts, apply-patch.ts); the capability registry is packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts (an auto-review entry may already exist as a planned capability, Codex provider only, default on); the tool_call gate is in packages/integrations/pi/src/extension.ts.
The design research is in /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw96z5n3-mw6f.md: read it first; it cites Codex's own guardian sources.

Intent requirements (verbatim): Maintainer: "the new codex provider should have auto review and context_management"; "the codex-auto-review should work similarly to how codex's work": auto-review follows Codex's own auto-review behaviour (what triggers a review, what the reviewer sees, how allow, deny and failure are handled), not a rule list the user must write. Default design: Pi has no sandbox, so a classifier stands in for escalation: bash commands outside a read-only safe set, writes outside the project root, network use, and tools whose annotations need approval go to review; everything else runs. Request: model codex-auto-review, Codex policy template plus policy text (replaceable or extendable by config), a budgeted transcript (Codex caps: 10k message and 10k tool tokens, last 40 entries) labelled untrusted, the action as JSON, strict GuardianAssessment schema (risk_level, user_authorization, outcome, rationale), 90 s timeout. Decisions: allow runs; deny returns Codex rejection text and instructions to the model; timeout is not a denial and allows one retry; failures deny closed; a breaker stops the turn after 3 consecutive or 10 total denials; a one-retry user override like /approve. Everything is modular and can be turned off on its own. The auto-review reviewer uses codex-auto-review.
Testing rule: unit tests with recorded or synthesized fixtures only; the reviewer request is made through an injectable client so tests never reach a network.

notes:
- The brief said an `auto-review` capability might already exist as a planned entry. It did not, so I added it, placed after `context-management`.
- `bun fmt` added blank lines after the headings in Codex's markdown texts. The wording is verbatim.
- The `/approve` retry is reviewed again. A second timeout of the same action gets a "do not retry again" message, which is not in Codex.
- Differences from Codex, documented in `providers.md`:
  - The assessment is strict. All four fields are required; Codex fills missing ones in.
  - The reviewer has no tools or reused session.
  - The classifier is deliberately broad, since Pi has no sandbox.
- Not verified: the live Codex backend request shape. It follows Pi's own Codex request and was only tested with stubs, as the brief requires. If the backend rejects `codex-auto-review` or the strict schema, every review fails closed.
- Possible later improvements:
  - A symlink-aware root check.
  - A per-turn denial notice of counts.
  - A config key for the timeout.
